faqs.question: Why should I run how to flush dns cache windows?
faqs.answer: When a website updates its IP address or migrates to a new server, your operating system continues caching the outdated IP until the TTL expires. Flushing your DNS forces your system to fetch fresh records immediately.

faqs.question: Does flushing DNS delete my browser history or cookies?
faqs.answer: No. Flushing the DNS cache only clears temporary IP mapping tables stored by the OS resolver. It does not touch browser bookmarks, passwords, or cookies.

faqs.question: Do I need administrator privileges to flush DNS?
faqs.answer: On Windows, running CMD as administrator is recommended. On macOS and Linux, you must use sudo to restart mDNSResponder or systemd-resolved.

sections.heading: What Is the Local DNS Cache?
sections.content: Every modern operating system maintains a temporary database known as the DNS resolver cache. When you visit a website, your computer saves the resolved IP address locally so it doesn't have to query external DNS resolvers on every single page load.
